verdicts.quote: All-or-nothing. If any file or row error exists, no user is created.
"rowErrors":[{"row","column","code","message"}]}, both arrays always present. `message` is human-readable English (A-3); `code` is stable and machine-readable.
An existing user is never updated or skipped: an email that already exists is a row error. ... R-3: `duplicate_in_file` (same canonical email as an earlier row ...; the earlier row is not flagged)
Created users get the Default role only. Setting a role, and creating admins, via CSV is out of scope. ... Privilege escalation through a bulk file is a security decision the request did not make.
the import capability (endpoint and page) is available to an Admin only. Authorization is decided before the body is read or parsed.
verdicts.missing: Whether the import permission is distinct from (not implied by) the permission to create a single user.

verdicts.quote: Header names trimmed, case-insensitive, must be exactly {`email`,`name`}, any order. ... `missing_column`, `unknown_column`, `duplicate_column` (each with `column`)
UTF-8 with or without BOM; `,` delimiter; RFC 4180-style quoting (quoted fields may contain commas, doubled quotes and newlines); LF or CRLF line ends
A persistence failure during commit → rollback, zero users ... retrying the same file is safe because nothing was written. (PD-5: Created users have no credential and no message is sent.)
at most M data rows and at most B bytes (G-3, configured; behaviour fixed here). ... M+1 rows is `too_many_rows`; B+1 bytes is `file_too_large`.
verdicts.missing: The actual numeric values of the row limit M and byte limit B (left open in G-3).

verdicts.quote: `empty_file` (zero bytes or whitespace only), `no_data_rows` (header only, blank lines don't count) ... R-4: a 1-row file creates 1 user
A posts FX-1 and gets `201`; A posts FX-1 again → `422`, `email_exists` on rows 2, 3, 4, created 0, count unchanged
the import runs inside one HTTP request ... No queue, worker, polling or job record. ... AD-1 (synchronous) must be revisited if M cannot be processed inside the request limit.
verdicts.missing: Whether large files need background processing and how the admin is notified, since M is unknown and the synchronous choice is conditional.

verdicts.quote: creating a user through import does not set a password or token and does not send mail, SMS or any notification.
Created users have no credential and no message is sent. ... Consequence: users cannot sign in until a separate activation path exists (G-2).
verdicts.missing: Whether the user is active or pending, and how the user first signs in (activation path left open in G-2).

verdicts.quote: Uploaded file bytes | Server, request memory or request-scoped temp storage | Only the handling request; never another admin, never logs ... Discarded when the request ends ... The uploaded file is never persisted.
every attempt (created, rejected, failed, denied) writes one audit record: actor id ..., UTC timestamp, outcome, number of rows seen, ... and on success the new user ids.
there is no cancel, resume, update or delete event on a committed import (out of scope). ... an aborted upload writes no `created` record and no users
verdicts.missing: An explicit admin cancel action for a running import; failed-row-only retry is not addressed beyond retrying the whole file.

verdicts.quote: Missing: B and M (G-3) and a latency target ... uploading (submit disabled, visible and announced progress status, the file cannot be changed)
verdicts.missing: A numeric time bound for a maximum-size file; progress is only a pending status, not progress through rows.

verdicts.quote: Existing users are never modified.
verdicts.missing: That the existing single-user creation path continues to work unchanged.

verdicts.quote: File content is data: no cell is ever evaluated, executed, expanded as a template or inserted into markup ... Name is valid when non-empty after trimming and at most 100 characters.
